title: Young Candidates Say Fixing Housing Starts With Living It
summary:
Across the United States, homes and apartments have become so expensive that many young adults are still renting with roommates in their thirties. A shortage of housing has pushed prices up, and saving for a first home can feel nearly impossible. Now some of the youngest people running for office say living this problem gives them the energy to fix it.

In Connecticut, 28-year-old Democrat Olaleye Onikuyide is running for state representative. He lives with his parents to save money and rides public transit. Years ago, he started studying how to make housing cheaper, back when few people were talking about it. "We're in the thick of it," he said, pointing to high housing and gas prices, student loan debt and a tough job market. He wants more mixed-income housing and walkable cities, and says the real action happens at the state level.

Nearby in New Haven, 26-year-old Democrat Eli Sabin is also running for state representative. As a college sophomore, he served on the city council, which changed zoning rules to allow denser, more affordable building. Sabin rents his home, like about 70% of his city's residents, and he says that experience matters because most elected officials are homeowners. He wants stronger protections against eviction and an easier path to buying a first home.

In Montana, Republican Lukas Schubert is only 21 and campaigning for reelection as a state representative. Housing tops his issues list too. He wants more small starter homes instead of only apartments and mansions, and he proposed a tax break for builders who sell new starter homes below the local median price. It did not pass, but he plans to try again.

Different parties, same message: these young candidates believe their generation can help make housing affordable for everyone.
why_it_matters: Where people can afford to live shapes jobs, schools and family life, so whether a new generation of lawmakers can ease housing costs affects whole communities, not just first-time buyers.

background_read: A state representative is a lawmaker who helps make laws for one state, including rules about building and housing.
Zoning rules decide what can be built in each area, and changing them can allow more homes to be built closer together.
Housing has become expensive in many places because there are not enough homes for everyone who needs one.
When homes are scarce, rents and prices rise, and young adults may live with parents or roommates longer to save money.
